definitions.explanation: Humble form of {聞|き}く (to ask). Used when politely asking someone of higher status.
Humble form of {訪|たず}ねる or {行|い}く. Used when humbly stating you will visit someone's place.
Humble form of {聞|き}く (to hear). Used when politely saying you heard something.

examples.japanese: ちょっとうかがいたいのですが。
examples.english: I'd like to ask you something.
examples.notes: Very polite way to start a question

examples.japanese: {明日|あした}、お{宅|たく}にうかがいます。
examples.english: I will visit your home tomorrow.
examples.notes: Humble way to say 'I will come to your place'

examples.japanese: お{名前|なまえ}をうかがってもよろしいですか。
ご{都合|つごう}のいい{時間|じかん}をうかがいたいのですが。
examples.english: I'd like to ask what time is convenient for you.

examples.japanese: {来週|らいしゅう}、{会社|かいしゃ}にうかがってもよろしいでしょうか。
examples.english: Would it be all right if I visit the office next week?

examples.japanese: ご{意見|いけん}をうかがいたいです。
examples.english: I would like to ask for your opinion.

examples.japanese: {道|みち}をうかがってもよろしいですか。

examples.english: I will visit in the afternoon.

examples.japanese: ご{自宅|じたく}にうかがってもいいですか。
{何時|なんじ}にうかがえばよろしいですか。
お{話|はなし}はうかがっています。
お{噂|うわさ}はかねがねうかがっております。
examples.english: I have heard much about you.

examples.japanese: {先生|せんせい}からうかがいました。
{事情|じじょう}はうかがっております。
examples.english: I have heard about the circumstances.

examples.japanese: その{件|けん}はすでにうかがっています。
examples.english: I have already heard about that matter.

notes:
TRANSITIVITY: {他動詞|たどうし} (transitive). Pattern: Xをうかがう / Xにうかがう.

ASPECT: ている indicates ongoing or completed action. うかがっている = 'have heard/asked.'

KEIGO (HUMBLE): This verb is {謙譲語|けんじょうご} (humble language). Use when:
・Asking someone of higher status
・Visiting someone's home or office
・Referring to information you received from someone respected

EQUIVALENTS:
・うかがう (humble) ↔ {聞|き}く (neutral) ↔ お{聞|き}きになる (honorific)
・うかがう (humble) ↔ {訪|たず}ねる/{行|い}く (neutral) ↔ いらっしゃる (honorific)

COMMON PATTERNS:
・うかがいたいのですが (I'd like to ask...)
・うかがってもよろしいですか (May I ask...)
・お{話|はなし}をうかがう (hear what someone has to say)

WRITING: Can be written as {伺|うかが}う but hiragana is common.
